skill.name: flagship
skill.description: Build, debug, or review code that uses Cloudflare Flagship feature flags from Workers, OpenFeature SDKs, the evaluation API, or Wrangler. Use for the Flagship binding, targeting rules, percentage rollouts and A/B splits, kill switches, local flag stores, and flag-related API tokens.
skill.summary: Integrate and troubleshoot Cloudflare Flagship feature flags, and plan rollouts with targeting rules, percentage splits, and kill switches.
skill.author: cloudflare

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown references, diagnostic examples, or instructions to redact sensitive data. The Wrangler guidance includes package execution and flag imports that can overwrite local state. Live flag updates lack an explicit user approval step.

remediation.issue: Type generation can fetch and execute Wrangler when it is not installed locally.
remediation.suggestion: Use the project-locked Wrangler executable, and ask before installing dependencies or generating files.

remediation.issue: Pulling flags can copy remote rules into the workspace and overwrite matching local flags.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer synthetic local flags for tests. Before pulling, confirm the source app and state directory with the user and explain what will be overwritten.

remediation.issue: Live flag changes can replace rules or clear fields without a separate user approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Show the target app, current flag, proposed changes, and rollback plan. Obtain explicit approval before any live write, and do not bypass confirmation prompts.

content.user_title: Build and Debug Cloudflare Flagship Feature Flags
content.value_statement: Feature flags can return unexpected values when local state, defaults, or targeting rules differ from what you expect. Flagship guides integration, evaluation diagnostics, and rollout planning using Cloudflare documentation and generated types.
actual_capabilities: Guide setup of a Flagship binding and typed flag evaluation inside a Cloudflare Worker.
Compare OpenFeature providers and HTTP evaluation, including the token permissions each approach needs.
Explain unexpected values using evaluation reasons, error codes, and safe defaults.
Explain how to seed and inspect local flag stores for development and testing.
Review rule order and stable bucketing for percentage rollouts and A/B splits.
Explain kill switches and how to retire a flag after removing its evaluation code.
limitations: Code and command syntax depend on your installed versions and current Cloudflare documentation.
The skill does not provide Cloudflare credentials or independently verify your deployed flag configuration.
Local development uses a separate flag store by default, so a local result does not prove what production serves.

use_cases.title: Add a flag to a Worker
use_cases.description: Choose a typed binding method and a fallback that preserves current behavior when evaluation fails.

use_cases.title: Explain a failing local flag test
use_cases.description: Check whether the flag exists in the test store and use evaluation details to distinguish missing flags from type or context errors.

use_cases.title: Review a staged release
use_cases.description: Check rule order, stable bucketing, and the default variant before proposing rollout thresholds and a rollback plan.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Worker binding
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to evaluate the Boolean flag [flag key] with a Flagship binding. Use a default that preserves [current behavior]. Suggest changes without running commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Adding a flag to a Cloudflare Worker.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose an unexpected default
prompt_templates.prompt: My local Worker returns [default] for [flag key]. Review [redacted evaluation details] and suggest checks for the local store, flag type, and evaluation context.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Diagnosing local flag behavior without accessing a live account.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an evaluation approach
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare an OpenFeature server provider with the HTTP evaluation API for [runtime]. Explain context support and the minimum token permissions. Do not request credentials.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Choosing an integration outside Cloudflare Workers.

prompt_templates.title: Review an A/B rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [redacted rules] for a [proposed split] rollout. Check rule order, bucketing, replacement risks, and rollback. Show the proposed changes without applying them.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Reviewing a production rollout before seeking approval.

output_examples.input: Why does my local Worker always return the default for a flag?
output: Check whether the flag exists in the local store used by the running tool.
Use the detailed evaluation method to distinguish a missing flag from a type or context error.
Seed a synthetic local flag and repeat the check before testing against a remote app.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed 10 percent rollout that must preserve our staff targeting rule.
output: Keep the staff rule before the broader percentage rule and use a stable targeting key.
Avoid replacing all rules when adding the rollout. Verify that the existing rules remain in the proposed configuration.
Confirm that the default variant restores current behavior before relying on the kill switch.

best_practices: Check the current Cloudflare documentation and generated binding types before suggesting code or commands.
Use stable targeting identifiers and include only the context attributes that the rules need.
Review current rules and obtain approval before making changes to a live flag.
anti_patterns: Embedding a Flagship API token in a public client application.
Using a changing or missing targeting key for a rollout that needs consistent assignments.
Replacing the full rule set when you only intend to add or edit one rule.

faq.question: Does a Worker binding need an API token?
faq.answer: No. The binding authenticates automatically inside the Worker.

faq.question: Which token permission do I need outside Workers?
faq.answer: Use Evaluate for remote evaluation with OpenFeature. Local evaluation in a server SDK needs Read instead.

faq.question: Why does my local flag return the default?
faq.answer: The local flag store starts empty. A missing flag, type mismatch, or invalid context can also cause a default result.

faq.question: What happens when a user misses a rollout percentage?
faq.answer: Evaluation moves to the next rule. Put specific rules before broad rules and use a stable bucketing value.

faq.question: What does disabling a flag do?
faq.answer: A disabled flag serves its default variant regardless of targeting rules. Changes can take up to 30 seconds to propagate.

faq.question: Can I evaluate a flag without an SDK?
faq.answer: Yes. The HTTP Evaluation API supports GET for scalar context and POST for structured context.
